_about: Public-domain David Bogue, Independent minister at Gosport and a founder of the London Missionary Society, for the Word Hoard: An Essay on the Divine Authority of the New Testament, his Theological Lectures, and his sermons and addresses, among them The Great Importance of Having Right Sentiments in Religion, The Diffusion of Divine Truth, and his sermon on the deaths of three missionaries. Texts are from Internet Archive scans. Added 2026-10-23 by lane A, round 134 (my pick); Adam may veto the whole shelf. Every printing dated before 1930, so public domain in the US. No uids minted.

bogue-right-sentiments: The great importance of having right sentiments in religion: a sermon, preached at an association of ministers, ... on Tuesday, the 29th of July, 1788. By the Rev. David Bogue, ...  1788 (catalogued 1788)

bogue-diffusion-divine-truth: The diffusion of divine truth. A sermon, preached before the Religious Tract Society, on Lord's Day, May 18, 1800. ... By David Bogue.  1800 (catalogued 1800)
bogue-divine-authority-nt: An essay on the divine authority of the New Testament ([n. p.], 1804)
bogue-death-of-missionaries: Sermon on the death of the Reverend George Cran, Augustus Desgranges, and Jonathan Brain, missionaries in India from the London Missionary Society : preached at Gosport, March 17, 1811 / by David Bogue (Boston : Samuel T. Armstrong, 1811)
